subs.title: One-One, Onto, Inverse and Number of Functions

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=|x-1|\). Then
If \(f(x)=\cos(\log x)\), then \(f(x)f(y)-\dfrac12\left[f\left(\dfrac xy\right)+f(xy)\right]\) has the value
questions.sol: With \(A=\log x\), \(B=\log y\): \(\cos A\cos B-\tfrac12[\cos(A-B)+\cos(A+B)]=0\).

questions.q: The domain of definition of the function \(y=\dfrac1{\log_{10}(1-x)}+\sqrt{x+2}\) is
Which of the following functions is periodic ?
opts: \(f(x)=x-[x]\), where \([x]\) denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to the real number \(x\)
questions.sol: \(x-[x]\) is the fractional part, periodic with period \(1\). \(\sin\frac1x\) and \(x\cos x\) do not repeat.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\sin x\) and \(g(x)=\ln|x|\). If the ranges of the composition functions \(fog\) and \(gof\) are \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) respectively, then
questions.sol: \(fog=\sin(\ln|x|)\) takes every value in \([-1,1]\) since \(\ln|x|\) covers \(R\). \(gof=\ln|\sin x|\) with \(0<|\sin x|\le1\) has range \((-\infty,0]\).
\(f\) is increasing, so \(f(x)=f^{-1}(x)\) exactly when \(f(x)=x\): \(x^2+2x=x\) gives \(x=0,-1\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=|px-q|+r|x|\), \(x\in(-\infty,\infty)\) where \(p>0\), \(q>0\), \(r>0\) assumes its minimum value only on one point if
questions.sol: The slopes on \(x<0\), \(0<x<\frac qp\), \(x>\frac qp\) are \(-(p+r)\), \(r-p\), \(p+r\). If \(r=p\) the middle piece is flat and the minimum is attained on a whole interval; if \(r\ne p\) it is attained at a single corner.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\) be defined for all \(x>0\) and be continuous. If \(f(x)\) satisfy \(f\left(\dfrac xy\right)=f(x)-f(y)\) for all \(x,y\) and \(f(e)=1\), then
questions.sol: The continuous solutions of \(f\left(\frac xy\right)=f(x)-f(y)\) are \(f(x)=k\ln x\); \(f(e)=1\) gives \(k=1\). Then \(f\) is unbounded, \(f\left(\frac1x\right)\to\infty\) and \(x\ln x\to0\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2-1}{x^2+1}\), for every real number \(x\), then the minimum value of \(f\)
opts: does not exist because \(f\) is unbounded
is not attained even though \(f\) is bounded
questions.sol: \(f(x)=1-\dfrac2{x^2+1}\) is least when \(x^2+1\) is least, i.e. at \(x=0\): \(f(0)=-1\).

opts: does not exist because \(f\) is not one-one
does not exist because \(f\) is not onto.
questions.sol: \(f\) is a bijection of \(R\); \(y=3x-5\) gives \(x=\dfrac{y+5}3\).

questions.q: If \(g(f(x))=|\sin x|\) and \(f(g(x))=\left(\sin\sqrt x\right)^2\), then
questions.sol: For (a): \(g(f(x))=\sqrt{\sin^2x}=|\sin x|\) and \(f(g(x))=\sin^2\sqrt x\). Both conditions hold.

questions.q: The number of values of \(x\) where the function \(f(x)=\cos x+\cos(\sqrt2x)\) attains its maximum is
questions.sol: The maximum \(2\) needs \(x=2n\pi\) and \(\sqrt2x=2m\pi\), i.e. \(\sqrt2n=m\) for integers, possible only for \(n=m=0\). So only \(x=0\).

questions.q: If the function \(f:[1,\infty)\to[1,\infty)\) is defined by \(f(x)=2^{x(x-1)}\), then \(f^{-1}(x)\) is
questions.sol: \(y=2^{x(x-1)}\) gives \(x^2-x-\log_2y=0\), so \(x=\dfrac{1\pm\sqrt{1+4\log_2y}}2\); as \(x\ge1\) take the \(+\) sign.

questions.q: Let \(f(\theta)=\sin\theta(\sin\theta+\sin3\theta)\) then \(f(\theta)\)
questions.sol: \(\sin\theta+\sin3\theta=2\sin2\theta\cos\theta\), so \(f(\theta)=\sin2\theta\cdot2\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin^22\theta\ge0\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\) be any function. Defined \(g:R\to R\) by \(g(x)=|f(x)|\) for all \(x\). Then \(g\) is
questions.sol: \(|\cdot|\) is continuous, so \(|f|\) is continuous whenever \(f\) is. With \(f(x)=x\): \(g=|x|\) is neither onto, one-one, nor differentiable at \(0\).

questions.q: The domain of definition of the function \(f(x)\) given by the equation \(2^x+2^y=2\) is
questions.sol: \(2^y=2-2^x\) must be positive: \(2^x<2\), i.e. \(x<1\).

questions.q: Let \(E=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and \(F=\{1,2\}\), then the number of onto functions from \(E\) to \(F\) is
questions.sol: All functions: \(2^4=16\); the two constant functions are not onto. \(16-2=14\).

questions.q: The domain of definition of \(f(x)=\dfrac{\log_2(x+3)}{x^2+3x+2}\) is
If \(f:[1,\infty)\to[2,\infty)\) is given by \(f(x)=x+\dfrac1x\), then \(f^{-1}(x)\) equals
questions.sol: \(y=x+\frac1x\) gives \(x^2-yx+1=0\), \(x=\dfrac{y\pm\sqrt{y^2-4}}2\); \(x\ge1\) needs the \(+\) sign.

questions.q: Let \(g(x)=1+x-[x]\) and \(f(x)=\begin{cases}-1,&x<0\\0,&x=0\\1,&x>0\end{cases}\) then for all \(x\), \(f(g(x))\) is equal to
Let \(f(x)=\dfrac{\alpha x}{x+1}\), \(x\ne-1\), then for what value of \(\alpha\) is \(f(f(x))=x\) ?
questions.sol: \(f(f(x))=\dfrac{\alpha^2x}{(\alpha+1)x+1}=x\) for all \(x\) needs \(\alpha+1=0\) and \(\alpha^2=1\): \(\alpha=-1\).

questions.q: Suppose \(f(x)=(x+1)^2\) for \(x\ge-1\). If \(g(x)\) is the function whose graph is the reflection of the graph of \(f(x)\) with respect to the line \(y=x\), then \(g(x)\) equals
questions.sol: The reflection in \(y=x\) is the inverse: \(y=(x+1)^2\), \(x\ge-1\) gives \(x=\sqrt y-1\), \(y\ge0\).

questions.q: Let function \(f:R\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=2x+\sin x\) for \(x\in R\). Then \(f\) is
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=2+\cos x>0\), so \(f\) is strictly increasing (one-one); it is continuous with \(f\to\pm\infty\) as \(x\to\pm\infty\), so onto.

questions.q: The domain of the derivative of the function \(f(x)=\begin{cases}\tan^{-1}x,&\text{if }|x|\le1\\[2pt]\dfrac12(|x|-1),&\text{if }|x|>1\end{cases}\) is
questions.sol: At \(x=1\): \(f(1)=\frac\pi4\) but \(f(1^+)=0\); at \(x=-1\): \(f(-1)=-\frac\pi4\) but \(f(-1^-)=0\). \(f\) is discontinuous, hence not differentiable, at \(\pm1\) and differentiable elsewhere.

questions.q: If \(f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\), and \(f(x)=\dfrac x{1+x}\), then \(f\) is
questions.sol: \(f(x)=1-\dfrac1{1+x}\) is increasing (one-one) with range \([0,1)\ne[0,\infty)\).

questions.q: Domain of definition of the function \(f(x)=\sqrt{\sin^{-1}(2x)+\dfrac\pi6}\) for real valued \(x\), is
questions.sol: \(-\frac\pi6\le\sin^{-1}(2x)\le\frac\pi2\) gives \(-\frac12\le2x\le1\).

questions.q: Range of the function \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2+x+2}{x^2+x+1}\); \(x\in R\) is
questions.sol: \(f=1+\dfrac1{x^2+x+1}\) and \(x^2+x+1\in\left[\frac34,\infty\right)\), so \(f\in\left(1,1+\frac43\right]\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\sin x+\cos x\), \(g(x)=x^2-1\), then \(g(f(x))\) is invertible in the domain
questions.sol: \(g(f(x))=(\sin x+\cos x)^2-1=\sin2x\), which is one-one when \(-\frac\pi2\le2x\le\frac\pi2\).

questions.q: \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x,&\text{if }x\text{ is rational}\\0,&\text{if }x\text{ is irrational}\end{cases}\) and \(g(x)=\begin{cases}0,&\text{if }x\text{ is rational}\\x,&\text{if }x\text{ is irrational}\end{cases}\). Then \(f-g\) is
questions.sol: \((f-g)(x)=x\) for rational \(x\) and \(-x\) for irrational \(x\). Rationals map onto rationals and irrationals onto irrationals, each one-one, so \(f-g\) is a bijection of \(R\).

questions.q: \(X\) and \(Y\) are two sets and \(f:X\to Y\). If \(\{f(c)=y;\ c\subset X,\ y\subset Y\}\), then the true statement is
questions.sol: The given correspondence pairs each \(c\subset X\) with its image \(y=f(c)\), so going back from \(f(a)\) returns \(a\) for \(a\subset X\): \(f^{-1}(f(a))=a\), \(a\subset X\). Statements (b), (d) would need \(f\) to be onto, and (a) does not say where \(a\) lies.

questions.q: If \(F(x)=\left(f\left(\dfrac x2\right)\right)^2+\left(g\left(\dfrac x2\right)\right)^2\) where \(f''(x)=-f(x)\) and \(g(x)=f'(x)\) and given that \(F(5)=5\), then \(F(10)\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(F'(x)=f\left(\frac x2\right)f'\left(\frac x2\right)+g\left(\frac x2\right)g'\left(\frac x2\right)\). Since \(f'=g\) and \(g'=f''=-f\), this is \(fg-gf=0\). So \(F\) is constant: \(F(10)=F(5)=5\).

questions.q: Let \(S=\{1,2,3,4\}\). The total number of unordered pairs of disjoint subsets of \(S\) is equal to
questions.sol: Each element goes to \(A\), to \(B\) or to neither: \(3^4=81\) ordered pairs \((A,B)\). Only \((\phi,\phi)\) has \(A=B\); the other \(80\) pair up, so unordered pairs \(=\dfrac{81-1}2+1=41\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=x^2\) and \(g(x)=\sin x\) for all \(x\in R\). Then the set of all \(x\) satisfying \((fogogof)(x)=(gogof)(x)\), where \((fog)(x)=f(g(x))\), is
questions.sol: With \(t=\sin(\sin x^2)\) the equation is \(t^2=t\), so \(t=0\) or \(1\). \(t=1\) needs \(\sin x^2=\frac\pi2>1\), impossible. \(t=0\) gives \(\sin x^2=0\), \(x^2=n\pi\), \(n=0,1,2,\ldots\)

questions.q: The function \(f:[0,3]\to[1,29]\), defined by \(f(x)=2x^3-15x^2+36x+1\), is
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=6(x-2)(x-3)\): \(f\) rises on \([0,2]\) from \(f(0)=1\) to \(f(2)=29\), then falls to \(f(3)=28\). Range \([1,29]\) (onto), but not one-one.

questions.q: If the function \(f:R\to R\) is defined by \(f(x)=|x|(x-\sin x)\), then which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.sol: \(f\) is odd. For \(x>0\): \(f=x^2-x\sin x\), \(f'=x(1-\cos x)+(x-\sin x)>0\), so \(f\) is strictly increasing on \(R\); it is continuous and \(f\to\pm\infty\), hence onto.

questions.q: \(y=f(x)=\dfrac{x+2}{x-1}\) then
questions.sol: \(y(x-1)=x+2\) gives \(x=\dfrac{y+2}{y-1}=f(y)\). \(f(1)\) is undefined; \(f'(x)=-\dfrac3{(x-1)^2}<0\), so \(y\) decreases; \(f\) is a ratio of polynomials.

questions.q: Let \(g(x)\) be a function defined on \([-1,1]\). If the area of the equilateral triangle with two of its vertices at \((0,0)\) and \([x,g(x)]\) is \(\sqrt3/4\), then the function \(g(x)\) is
questions.sol: Area \(\frac{\sqrt3}4(\text{side})^2=\frac{\sqrt3}4\) gives side \(1\): \(x^2+g(x)^2=1\). So \(g=\sqrt{1-x^2}\) or \(g=-\sqrt{1-x^2}\); (a) is not a single-valued function.

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\cos[\pi^2]x+\cos[-\pi^2]x\), where \([x]\) stands for the greatest integer function, then
Let \(f:(0,1)\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{b-x}{1-bx}\), where \(b\) is a constant such that \(0<b<1\). Then
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=\dfrac{b^2-1}{(1-bx)^2}<0\), so \(f\) decreases from \(f(0^+)=b\) to \(f(1^-)=-1\): its range \((-1,b)\) is not the codomain \(R\). \(f\) is not onto, hence not invertible, and the other statements (which use \(f^{-1}\)) fail.

questions.q: Let \(f:(-1,1)\to R\) be such that \(f(\cos4\theta)=\dfrac2{2-\sec^2\theta}\) for \(\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi4\right)\cup\left(\dfrac\pi4,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then the values of \(f\left(\dfrac13\right)\) is (are)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac2{2-\sec^2\theta}=\dfrac{2\cos^2\theta}{\cos2\theta}=1+\dfrac1{\cos2\theta}\). \(\cos4\theta=\frac13\) gives \(\cos^22\theta=\frac23\), \(\cos2\theta=\pm\sqrt{\frac23}\) (both occur on the given set). So \(f\left(\frac13\right)=1\pm\sqrt{\frac32}\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=\sin\left(\dfrac\pi6\sin\left(\dfrac\pi2\sin x\right)\right)\) for all \(x\in R\) and \(g(x)=\dfrac\pi2\sin x\) for all \(x\in R\). Let \((fog)(x)\) denote \(f(g(x))\) and \((gof)(x)\) denote \(g(f(x))\). Then which of the following is (are) true?
opts: There is an \(x\in R\) such that \((gof)(x)=1\)
questions.sol: \(\frac\pi2\sin x\in\left[-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right]\), so \(\sin(\cdot)\in[-1,1]\) and \(f\in\left[-\frac12,\frac12\right]\); the same holds for \(fog\) because \(g\) also covers \(\left[-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right]\). Near \(0\): \(f\approx\frac\pi6\cdot\frac\pi2x\), \(g\approx\frac\pi2x\), ratio \(\frac\pi6\). \((gof)=1\) needs \(\sin f(x)=\frac2\pi\approx0.64\), but \(\sin f\le\sin\frac12\approx0.48\).

questions.q: Let \(f:R\to R\), \(g:R\to R\) and \(h:R\to R\) be differentiable functions such that \(f(x)=x^3+3x+2\), \(g(f(x))=x\) and \(h(g(g(x)))=x\) for all \(x\in R\). Then
Let \(y=\sqrt{\dfrac{(x+1)(x-3)}{(x-2)}}\). Find all the real values of \(x\) for which \(y\) takes real values.
questions.sol: Need \(\dfrac{(x+1)(x-3)}{x-2}\ge0\), \(x\ne2\). Sign scheme with critical points \(-1,2,3\): the expression is \(\ge0\) on \([-1,2)\) and \([3,\infty)\).

questions.q: Given \(A=\left\{x:\dfrac\pi6\le x\le\dfrac\pi3\right\}\) and \(f(x)=\cos x-x(1+x)\). Find \(f(A)\).
questions.sol: \(f'(x)=-\sin x-1-2x<0\) on \(A\), so \(f\) is decreasing and continuous: \(f(A)=\left[f\left(\frac\pi3\right),f\left(\frac\pi6\right)\right]\) with \(f\left(\frac\pi3\right)=\frac12-\frac\pi3\left(1+\frac\pi3\right)\), \(f\left(\frac\pi6\right)=\frac{\sqrt3}2-\frac\pi6\left(1+\frac\pi6\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)\) for all \(x\) and \(y\). Suppose \(f(5)=2\) and \(f'(0)=3\). Find \(f'(5)\).
questions.sol: \(f(5)=f(5)f(0)\) gives \(f(0)=1\). \(f'(5)=\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(5)f(h)-f(5)}h=f(5)\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac{f(h)-f(0)}h=f(5)f'(0)=6\).

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a one-one function with domain \(\{x,y,z\}\) and range \(\{1,2,3\}\). It is given that exactly one of the following statements is true and the remaining statements are false. \(f(x)=1\), \(f(y)\ne1\), \(f(z)\ne2\). Determine \(f^{-1}(1)\).
questions.sol:
If only \(f(x)=1\) is true then \(f(y)=1\) too — not one-one. If only \(f(y)
e1\) is true then \(f(x)
e1\) and \(f(z)=2\), so nothing maps to \(1\). So only \(f(z)
e2\) is true: \(f(y)=1\), \(f(z)=3\), \(f(x)=2\). Hence \(f^{-1}(1)=y\).

questions.q: Let \(R\) be the set of real numbers and \(f:R\to R\) be such that for all \(x\) and \(y\) in \(R\) \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le|x-y|^3\). Prove that \(f(x)\) is a constant.
questions.sol: For \(x\ne y\): \(\left|\dfrac{f(x)-f(y)}{x-y}\right|\le|x-y|^2\). Letting \(y\to x\) gives \(|f'(x)|\le0\), so \(f'(x)=0\) for every \(x\) and \(f\) is constant.

questions.q: Show that the value of \(\dfrac{\tan x}{\tan3x}\), wherever defined never lies between \(\dfrac13\) and \(3\).
questions.sol: With \(t=\tan x\): \(y=\dfrac{\tan x}{\tan3x}=\dfrac{1-3t^2}{3-t^2}\), so \(t^2=\dfrac{3y-1}{y-3}\). As \(t^2>0\) (at \(t=0\) the ratio is undefined), \(\dfrac{3y-1}{y-3}>0\), i.e. \(y<\frac13\) or \(y>3\).

questions.q: Find the natural number '\(a\)' for which \(\sum\limits_{k=1}^nf(a+k)=16(2^n-1)\), where the function '\(f\)' satisfies the relation \(f(x+y)=f(x)f(y)\) for all natural numbers \(x,y\) and further \(f(1)=2\).
Let \(\{x\}\) and \([x]\) denotes the fractional and integral part of a real number \(x\) respectively. Solve \(4\{x\}=x+[x]\).

A function \(f:R\to R\), where \(R\) is the set of real numbers, is defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{\alpha x^2+6x-8}{\alpha+6x-8x^2}\). Find the interval of values of \(\alpha\) for which \(f\) is onto. Is the function one-to-one for \(\alpha=3\) ? Justify your answer.
questions.sol:
\(y=f(x)\) gives \((\alpha+8y)x^2+6(1-y)x-(8+\alpha y)=0\). For onto, the discriminant must be \(\ge0\) for every real \(y\): \((9+8\alpha)y^2+(\alpha^2+46)y+(9+8\alpha)\ge0\) for all \(y\). This needs \(9+8\alpha>0\) and \((\alpha^2+46)^2-4(9+8\alpha)^2\le0\), i.e. \((\alpha-2)(\alpha-14)(\alpha+8)^2\le0\): \(2\le\alpha\le14\).
For \(\alpha=3\): \(f(x)=0\) when \(3x^2+6x-8=0\), which has two real roots, so \(f\) is not one-to-one.

questions.q: Let \(f(x)=Ax^2+Bx+C\) where \(A,B,C\) are real numbers. Prove that if \(f(x)\) is an integer whenever \(x\) is an integer, then the numbers \(2A\), \(A+B\) and \(C\) are all integers. Conversely, prove that if the numbers \(2A\), \(A+B\) and \(C\) are all integers, then \(f(x)\) is an integer whenever \(x\) is an integer.
questions.sol:
\(f(0)=C\), \(f(1)=A+B+C\), \(f(-1)=A-B+C\) are integers, so \(C\), \(A+B=f(1)-C\) and \(2A=f(1)+f(-1)-2C\) are integers.
Conversely \(f(x)=2A\cdot\dfrac{x(x-1)}2+(A+B)x+C\), and \(\dfrac{x(x-1)}2\) is an integer for integer \(x\), so \(f(x)\) is an integer.

questions.q: If \(f(x)=(a-x^n)^{1/n}\) where \(a>0\) and \(n\) is a positive integer, then \(f[f(x)]=x\).
questions.sol: \(f(f(x))=\left(a-\left[(a-x^n)^{1/n}\right]^n\right)^{1/n}=(x^n)^{1/n}=x\).

questions.q: The function \(f(x)=\dfrac{x^2+4x+30}{x^2-8x+18}\) is not one-to-one.
If \(f_1(x)\) and \(f_2(x)\) are defined by domains \(D_1\) and \(D_2\) respectively, then \(f_1(x)+f_2(x)\) is defined as on \(D_1\cap D_2\).
questions.sol: The sum needs both \(f_1(x)\) and \(f_2(x)\) to be defined, i.e. \(x\in D_1\cap D_2\).

questions.q: The values of \(f(x)=3\sin\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{\pi^2}{16}-x^2}\right)\) lie in the interval ............
questions.sol: \(\sqrt{\frac{\pi^2}{16}-x^2}\in\left[0,\frac\pi4\right]\) and \(\sin\) is increasing there, so \(f\in\left[0,3\sin\frac\pi4\right]\).

questions.q: The domain of the function \(f(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\log_2\dfrac{x^2}2\right)\) is given by ..................
questions.sol: \(-1\le\log_2\dfrac{x^2}2\le1\) gives \(\frac12\le\frac{x^2}2\le2\), i.e. \(1\le x^2\le4\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be a set of \(n\) distinct elements. Then the total number of distinct functions from \(A\) to \(A\) is .......... and out of these ........... are onto functions.
questions.sol: Each of the \(n\) elements has \(n\) possible images: \(n^n\) functions. A function from a finite set to itself is onto exactly when it is a bijection: \(n!\).

questions.q: If \(f(x)=\sin\log\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{4-x^2}}{1-x}\right)\), then the domain of \(f(x)\) is ........
If \(f(x)=\sin^2x+\sin^2\left(x+\dfrac\pi3\right)+\cos x\cos\left(x+\dfrac\pi3\right)\) and \(g\left(\dfrac54\right)=1\), then \((gof)(x)=\) ........
questions.sol: \(f=1-\frac12\left[\cos2x+\cos\left(2x+\frac{2\pi}3\right)\right]+\frac12\left[\cos\left(2x+\frac\pi3\right)+\frac12\right]\) and \(\cos2x+\cos\left(2x+\frac{2\pi}3\right)=\cos\left(2x+\frac\pi3\right)\), so \(f\equiv\frac54\) and \(g(f(x))=g\left(\frac54\right)=1\).

questions.q: If \(f\) is an even function defined on \((-5,5)\) then the four real values of \(x\) satisfying the equation \(f(x)=f\left(\dfrac{x+1}{x+2}\right)\) are ............
questions.sol: As \(f\) is even, take \(\dfrac{x+1}{x+2}=x\) or \(-x\): \(x^2+x-1=0\) or \(x^2+3x+1=0\), giving \(x=\dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt5}2,\ \dfrac{-3\pm\sqrt5}2\).

questions.q:
Let the functions defined in column I have domain \(\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) and range \((-\infty,\infty)\).
Column IColumn II
(i) \(1+2x\)(A) onto but not one-one
(ii) \(\tan x\)(B) one to one but not onto
(C) one one and onto
(D) neither one-one nor onto.
questions.sol: \(1+2x\) is increasing with values only in \((1-\pi,1+\pi)\): one-one, not onto. \(\tan x\) increases from \(-\infty\) to \(\infty\) on \(\left(-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2\right)\): one-one and onto.

questions.q:
Let \(E_1=\left\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ne1\text{ and }\dfrac x{x-1}>0\right\}\) and \(E_2=\left\{x\in E_1:\sin^{-1}\left(\log_e\left(\dfrac x{x-1}\right)\right)\text{ is a real number}\right\}\). (Here, the inverse trigonometric function \(\sin^{-1}x\) assumes values in \(\left[-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right]\).) Let \(f:E_1\to\mathbb R\) be the function defined by \(f(x)=\log_e\left(\dfrac x{x-1}\right)\) and \(g:E_2\to\mathbb R\) be the function defined by \(g(x)=\sin^{-1}\left(\log_e\left(\dfrac x{x-1}\right)\right)\).
List-IList-II
P. The range of \(f\) is1. \(\left(-\infty,\dfrac1{1-e}\right]\cup\left[\dfrac e{e-1},\infty\right)\)
Q. The range of \(g\) contains2. \((0,1)\)
R. The domain of \(f\) contains3. \(\left[-\dfrac12,\dfrac12\right]\)
S. The domain of \(g\) is4. \((-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)\)
5. \(\left(-\infty,\dfrac e{e-1}\right]\)
6. \((-\infty,0)\cup\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac e{e-1}\right]\)
The correct option is :
questions.sol:
\(E_1=(-\infty,0)\cup(1,\infty)\), where \(\dfrac x{x-1}\in(0,1)\cup(1,\infty)\), so the range of \(f\) is \((-\infty,0)\cup(0,\infty)\) (P \(\to\) 4).

questions.q: For any real number \(x\), let \([x]\) denote the largest integer less than or equal to \(x\). Let \(f\) be a real valued function defined on the interval \([-10,10]\) by \(f(x)=\begin{cases}x-[x],&\text{if }[x]\text{ is odd}\\1+[x]-x,&\text{if }[x]\text{ is even}\end{cases}\) Then the value of \(\dfrac{\pi^2}{10}\displaystyle\int_{-10}^{10}f(x)\cos\pi x\,dx\) is ______ .
questions.sol: \(f\) and \(\cos\pi x\) both have period \(2\), so the integral is \(10\displaystyle\int_0^2f(x)\cos\pi x\,dx\). On \([0,1)\): \(f=1-x\); on \([1,2)\): \(f=x-1\). \(\displaystyle\int_0^1(1-x)\cos\pi x\,dx=\frac2{\pi^2}\) and \(\displaystyle\int_1^2(x-1)\cos\pi x\,dx=\frac2{\pi^2}\) (by parts). Total \(10\cdot\dfrac4{\pi^2}\), and \(\dfrac{\pi^2}{10}\cdot\dfrac{40}{\pi^2}=4\).

questions.q: Let \(X\) be a set with exactly \(5\) elements and \(Y\) be a set with exactly \(7\) elements. If \(\alpha\) is the number of one-one functions from \(X\) to \(Y\) and \(\beta\) is the number of onto functions from \(Y\) to \(X\), then the value of \(\dfrac1{5!}(\beta-\alpha)\) is ____ .

Let the function \(f:[0,1]\to R\) be defined by \(f(x)=\dfrac{4^x}{4^x+2}\). Then the value of \(f\left(\dfrac1{40}\right)+f\left(\dfrac2{40}\right)+f\left(\dfrac3{40}\right)+\ldots+f\left(\dfrac{39}{40}\right)-f\left(\dfrac12\right)\) is ______ .
questions.sol: \(f(x)+f(1-x)=\dfrac{4^x}{4^x+2}+\dfrac{4}{4+2\cdot4^x}=1\). The \(39\) terms form \(19\) pairs summing to \(1\) plus the middle term \(f\left(\frac12\right)\), which cancels. Value \(19\).

questions.q: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be a function such that \(f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)\) be a function such that \(g(x+y)=g(x)g(y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R\). If \(f\left(\dfrac{-3}5\right)=12\) and \(g\left(\dfrac{-1}3\right)=2\), then the value of \(\left(f\left(\dfrac14\right)+g(-2)-8\right)g(0)\) is ______.
questions.sol: For rational arguments \(f(x)=kx\) and \(g(x)=a^x\). \(-\frac35k=12\) gives \(k=-20\), \(f\left(\frac14\right)=-5\). \(a^{-1/3}=2\) gives \(a=\frac18\), \(g(-2)=64\), \(g(0)=1\). Value \((-5+64-8)\cdot1=51\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Let \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\) and \(X\) be the set of all relations \(R\) from \(S\) to \(S\) that satisfy both the following properties :
i. \(R\) has exactly \(6\) elements.
ii. For each \((a,b)\in R\), we have \(|a-b|\ge2\).
Let \(Y=\{R\in X:\text{The range of }R\text{ has exactly one element}\}\) and \(Z=\{R\in X:R\text{ is a function from }S\text{ to }S\}\).
Let \(n(A)\) denote the number of elements in a set \(A\).
If \(n(X)={}^mC_6\), then the value of \(m\) is ______.
questions.sol: Of the \(36\) ordered pairs, \(6\) have \(|a-b|=0\) and \(10\) have \(|a-b|=1\), leaving \(20\) allowed pairs. \(R\) is any \(6\) of them: \(n(X)={}^{20}C_6\), \(m=20\).

questions.q:
Question Stem
Let \(S=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}\) and \(X\) be the set of all relations \(R\) from \(S\) to \(S\) that satisfy both the following properties :
i. \(R\) has exactly \(6\) elements.
ii. For each \((a,b)\in R\), we have \(|a-b|\ge2\).
Let \(Y=\{R\in X:\text{The range of }R\text{ has exactly one element}\}\) and \(Z=\{R\in X:R\text{ is a function from }S\text{ to }S\}\).
Let \(n(A)\) denote the number of elements in a set \(A\).
If the value of \(n(Y)+n(Z)\) is \(k^2\), then \(|k|\) is ______.
questions.sol: For a fixed \(b\) at most \(4\) values of \(a\) satisfy \(|a-b|\ge2\), so a relation with \(6\) pairs cannot have a one-element range: \(n(Y)=0\). For a function, the number of allowed images of \(a=1,\ldots,6\) is \(4,3,3,3,3,4\): \(n(Z)=4\cdot3^4\cdot4=1296=36^2\). \(|k|=36\).

questions.q:
Let \(\mathbb N\) denote the set of all positive integers. Consider the sets \(A=\{1,2,3,4,5\}\) and \(B=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}\).
Let \(S\) be the set of all functions \(f:A\to B\) such that \(f(2)\ne2\) and \(f(4)\ne4\). Consider the set \(T=\{f\in S:\text{there exists a function }g:B\to\mathbb N\text{ such that }g(f(x))=2^x\text{ for all }x\in A\}\).
Then the number of elements in the set \(T\) is ______.
questions.sol: Such a \(g\) exists exactly when \(f\) is one-one (the values \(2^x\) are all different). One-one functions: \(7\cdot6\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3=2520\); with \(f(2)=2\): \(360\); with \(f(4)=4\): \(360\); with both: \(60\). \(2520-720+60\).
